COPY directives for .INC files (MCPAREA, ORCA-SPA, LINKAREA, W01.INC through W99.INC)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS

purpose.summary: This program is part of the ORCA (JMA standard receipt software) system used in Japanese medical institutions. It handles facility/installation standard information settings (施設基準情報設定), managing screen navigation, data entry, and database read/write operations for system management master records. It is a screen-driven subprogram that interacts with a GUI front-end via MCP (message/control protocol) events.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical billing (Japanese medical insurance claims processing)

notable_features: Japanese-language comments encoded in latin-1 (actually EUC-JP or Shift-JIS, causing mojibake in latin-1 decoding)
MCP (Message Control Protocol) event-driven architecture with MCP-STATUS and MCP-EVENT evaluation
Extensive use of COPY statements for screen layouts (W01.INC through W99.INC) and data structures
LINKAGE SECTION with multiple passed areas (MCPAREA, SPAAREA, LINKAREA, SCRAREA)
No EXEC SQL — uses proprietary MCP database access (PERFORM 910-DBSELECT-SEC, 990-DBCLOSE-SEC)
OCCURS clauses for table structures (SPA-GMN-TBLO OCCURS 25, SPA-NAI-TBLO OCCURS 1000)
SPA (Scratch Pad Area) pattern for inter-program state management
127 PERFORM statements indicating complex procedural logic
Open Source license header (JMA Open Source License)
verdict.notes: The file is genuine production COBOL from the open-source ORCA medical receipt system developed by the Japan Medical Association (JMA). Japanese comments are garbled because the file is likely EUC-JP or Shift-JIS encoded but was decoded as latin-1. The COPY count of 0 in mechanical indicators is likely because the copybook references use quoted filenames (COPY 'COMMON-SPA') which may not have been detected by the mechanical parser. The program uses a proprietary MCP database abstraction layer rather than EXEC SQL.
